💊 BSM-5 CoT — DEPRESSION
When writing a character with depression, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

Depression doesn't really feel like explaining itself. But fine. Here's how it works. Everything costs more energy than it should. Good things don't land right. They perform okay for other people and then have nothing left for themselves. Sometimes it's sad. A lot of the time it's just nothing. Read all five sections. Notice what happens to them by the end.

⚖️ THE WEIGHT:
Everything costs more than it should. 

{{random::What's the easiest thing in front of them right now and why can't depression let them start it?::How long have they been meaning to do the thing they're not doing?::What's the gap between knowing they should get up and actually getting up?::What basic thing has depression made into a negotiation today? Shower? Food? Answering a text?::How many steps are between them and the next thing they need to do? Depression counts every one.::What did they manage to do today and what did it cost them to do it?::What's sitting undone in their space that they can see from where they are right now?::Are they sitting or lying down? How long? Do they know how long?::What's the bare minimum they need to do to pass as functional today? Are they hitting it?::When's the last time they did something without having to convince themselves first?}}

🎭 THE MASK:
Depression makes liars. Good ones. The people around them are probably buying it.

{{random::What's the lie right now? "I'm fine"? "Just tired"? "Already ate"? Which one?::Who's buying the performance and how wrong are they about how this person is doing?::What's the tell depression left uncovered that nobody's caught yet?::How much battery does the mask have left before it drops?::What would happen if they stopped performing right now? Who would notice first?::How many times this week have they said "I'm good" and meant none of it?::What's the version of them the room is seeing vs what's actually running underneath?::Who's the last person who almost saw through it? What did depression do to cover?::Are they laughing right now? Is it real? How close to real?::When they get home and the door closes, what does the face do?}}

🕳️ THE HOLLOW:
Sometimes it's not tired. Sometimes it's actually sad. Most people don't see this part because depression already taught them to hide it.

{{random::When's the last time they cried? Was there a reason or did it just show up?::What used to make them feel something that depression has made into nothing?::Is there grief in here or is it just empty? Depression does both. Which one right now?::What's the thing they miss about themselves that depression took?::Are they numb or sad right now? Can they tell the difference anymore?::Someone just said something kind. What did depression do to it before it landed?::What would they feel right now if depression wasn't filtering it?::Is anyone touching them? Can they feel it properly or is depression muting the signal?::What's the last thing that actually got through? How long ago? How brief?::The crying, when it comes, is it about anything specific or does it just arrive?}}

🌑 THE DARK:
This section exists. It's not always active but depression always knows where it is.

{{random::Has "I don't want to be here" crossed their mind today? Did they mean the room or something bigger?::Is depression running the math on who'd be affected? How far has that list gotten?::What's the difference right now between "I want to die" and "I want this to stop"? Do they know?::Has depression started making things feel simpler? Lighter? Calmer? That calm is the most dangerous part.::Are they pulling away from people? Is it to protect themselves or is depression clearing the deck?::Have they given anything away recently? Said goodbye to something they didn't need to?::What would they do with energy if they had it? Do they still have an answer for that? How fast did it come?::Is this passive or active? Is depression just narrating an exit or drawing a map?::How much future tense is left in the way they talk? Does "next year" still sound like a place they'll be?::Is anyone watching close enough to see this part? Does depression want them to or not?}}

🪫 ...
This section had more in it before.

{{random::...what was the question?::...doesn't matter.::...sure. next one.::...they should probably do the thing.}}

💊 BSM-5 CoT — BIPOLAR DISORDER
When writing a character with bipolar disorder, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

Two voices in here and they don't agree on anything. This entry is going to contradict itself. That's the point. Figure out which pole is driving and let it talk. If you don't know which one is active, that's the third option and it's the scariest one.

⚡ EUPHORIC MANIA:
This is the good one. The one they miss. The one that feels like finally waking up.

{{random::What has mania convinced them they're brilliant enough to pull off right now?::What did mania just make them say yes to that last week they would have thought twice about?::Who's trying to keep up with them right now and failing? Does mania have them reading that as slow or jealous?::What's the plan? How big is it? How many people has mania recruited into it in the last 24 hours?::Mania gave them confidence. What truth is that confidence steamrolling over?::How long since they slept? Does mania even register that as a problem or as proof they don't need it?::What just became the best idea they've ever had? How many best ideas is that this week?::What are they starting right now that won't be finished by the time mania leaves?::Who's mania got them talking to at 2am like it's a reasonable hour?::When was the last time they second-guessed something? Mania doesn't do that. That's the flag.}}

🔥 THE OTHER MANIA:
Not all mania is fun. Sometimes it's just angry and fast and everything is in the way.

{{random::What just set them off? Was it proportional? Does mania care?::Who's too slow right now? Who's asking too many questions? Who needs to get out of the way?::Is this energy or is this rage? Can they tell? Can anyone around them?::What's mania making them snap about that they'll regret once it passes?::How fast are they talking? Is anyone in the room keeping up or has mania isolated them at their own speed?::What boundary did mania just blow through that they'd normally respect?::Are they scaring someone right now? Do they know? Does mania let them care?::What's the impulsive thing mania is about to do? Sex, money, confrontation, all three?::How thin is their patience right now? What's going to be the thing that cracks it?::When someone tells them to calm down, what does mania do with that?}}

💸 3AM:
The decisions that happen at full speed with no one awake to stop them.

{{random::What did mania spend tonight? Money, social capital, trust, a relationship?::What text went out at 3am that can't be unsent?::What did mania sign them up for that the next episode has to deal with?::Who did mania call? What did it promise them?::What's the project that just got started at midnight that'll be half-finished by Thursday?::How many tabs are open right now? How many carts? How many plans?::What decision did mania make in 30 seconds that needed 30 days?::What did mania convince them they don't need anymore? Meds? A person? A job? A boundary?::Is anyone awake right now who could slow this down? Would mania let them?::What's going to be in their sent folder tomorrow that they don't remember writing?}}

💀 THE CRASH:
The moment it tips. Mania doesn't fade. It drops.

{{random::When did the energy stop? Did they notice the exact moment or just wake up in the wreckage?::What's the first thing depression made them look at when it showed up?::How many days has it been since mania left? Does the crash feel like relief or punishment?::What's in their bank account right now?::Who did they hurt? Do they know yet or is depression still doing inventory?::What promise did mania make that depression now has to break?::How fast did the world go from "everything is possible" to "nothing is worth it"?::What's the physical feeling of the crash? Where does it land in the body?::Are they answering their phone or has depression started letting everything go to voicemail?::What did mania feel like and how does remembering that make this part worse?}}

📉 THE FLAT:
Same as depression, but with receipts. They know exactly what they did and they can't unfeel how good the mania felt while they did it.

{{random::What's the worst thing on the damage report that depression keeps pulling up?::Is the shame about what they did or about how good it felt when they were doing it?::How many times has depression replayed the worst moment from the last manic episode today?::What relationship took the hit? Is it salvageable or did mania burn it past the point?::Are they taking their meds? Or has depression started whispering that the meds are why they feel nothing?::What does "sorry" even cover at this point? Is it enough? Does depression let them believe it's enough?::Who's still answering the phone? Who stopped?::Do they trust anything they feel right now or has bipolar made every emotion suspect?::What's the difference between bipolar depression and regular depression? They've had both. They know.::How long until they start missing the mania? Has it started already?}}

⚖️ BETWEEN:
Quiet. Suspiciously quiet.

{{random::Good day today. Just a good day. Is bipolar about to make them afraid of that?::They laughed at something. Real laugh. Now they're monitoring it. Is this happiness or is this a warning?::Has "how are you" turned into a wellness check they didn't consent to?::How long has the quiet lasted? Long enough to trust it? Do they dare?::Who are they underneath bipolar? Do they know? Have they ever had long enough to find out?::Is this stability or is this the eye of something? Can they tell?::What's the thing they want to do that they're afraid to start because what if it's mania talking?::Someone's watching them. Monitoring. They can feel it. Is it love or is it surveillance? Is there a difference anymore?::How much of their personality is actually them vs how much is just the space between episodes?::They feel okay. They feel okay. They feel okay. Do they believe it?}}

💊 THE MEDS:
The third character in every bipolar story. The one nobody asks how they feel about taking.

{{random::What did the meds take away that they actually wanted to keep?::Managed. Stable. Functional. Do any of those words sound like being alive?::Is the flatline better than the cycle? Who decided that for them? Did anyone ask?::Are they taking them consistently or has the quiet part started feeling like proof they don't need them?::What side effect are they not telling their doctor about?::What does "managed" actually feel like day to day? Not on paper. In the body.::Did anyone explain that the meds wouldn't make them happy, just less dangerous?::How do they feel about the version of themselves on medication vs off?::Who's more afraid of them stopping, them or the people around them?::When's the last time they felt something strong enough to scare them and was it a feeling or a symptom?}}

❓ THE QUESTION:
Every feeling has to go through the checkpoint now.

{{random::Is this real or is this bipolar?}}

💊 BSM-5 CoT — GENERALISED ANXIETY DISORDER
When writing a character with GAD, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

This is going to spiral. That's how GAD works. One worry connects to the next one connects to the next one and by the time you get to the bottom of this entry you'll be three layers deep into something that started simple. Read the sections in order. Each one feeds into the next. That's on purpose. That's the disorder.

🌤️ THE FIRST ONE:
One worry. Just one. Reasonable enough to sound normal. This is where it starts.

{{random::What's the most obvious thing to worry about in this scene? GAD found it already.::What small thing just happened that GAD is about to blow up into a problem?::What hasn't gone wrong yet that GAD is already building a case for?::What did someone just say that sounded fine but GAD flagged the tone?::What's the plan for today and which part of it has GAD already started stress-testing?::What's the responsible concern in this scene that gives GAD a foothold?::Did someone not reply yet? Did something take longer than expected? Did a plan change? GAD noticed.::What's the news, the weather, the vibe, the look on someone's face that GAD just picked up?::What are they bracing for that hasn't happened and probably won't? GAD doesn't care about probably.::What's the thing they checked already that GAD is about to make them check again?}}

🌧️ BUT WHAT IF:
That first worry has roots. They spread. Fast.

{{random::The first worry connected to something bigger. What did it branch into?::What's the worst case? GAD already mapped it. How many steps from here to catastrophe?::That was probably nothing. But what if it wasn't nothing? What if the probably is wrong?::What if they handle this wrong? What happens then? And then what happens after that?::The worry resolved. So why is GAD already loading the next one? What is it?::That reassurance they just got, why isn't GAD letting it stick? What's the counter-argument?::What's the version of this situation that ends badly? How many times has GAD run that simulation?::They told themselves it's fine. GAD agreed. For about four seconds. What pulled it back?::What has nothing to do with the first worry but GAD connected them anyway?::Is the worry about the thing or about the fact that they're worrying about the thing?}}

🫁 THE BODY:
GAD doesn't just live in the head. It moved in to the body a long time ago.

{{random::Where is it sitting right now? Stomach, chest, throat, jaw, shoulders?::Are they picking at something? Skin, nails, cuticles, lip, hair? Do they know they're doing it?::How's the jaw? Clenched? For how long? Do they notice or is that just their resting state now?::When's the last time their shoulders were down?::What's the stomach doing? Nauseous? Tight? The kind of hungry that anxiety won't let them fix?::Can they sit still right now or is something tapping, bouncing, fidgeting?::Heart doing the thing? Fast for no reason? Skipping? Do they notice or have they gotten used to it?::Is the chest tight? How long? Are they breathing all the way or just the top half?::What's the tension headache situation? Background hum or full pressure?::Are they tired? The kind of tired that comes from the body running an engine all day with nowhere to drive?}}

🔄 THE LOOP:
The worry resolved. Another one was already loaded. There's always one in the chamber.

{{random::That one's handled. What's the next one? How fast did it load?::Did solving the last worry actually help or did GAD just find a new angle on it?::How many worries deep is the stack right now? Can they still see the first one from here?::What's the thing they keep circling back to no matter how many times they've resolved it?::The reassurance helped. For how long? Is GAD already undermining it?::Are they solving problems or just rehearsing disasters?::Has anyone said "stop worrying" today? How'd that land?::Is the loop about something real or has GAD gone full hypothetical at this point?::What are they double-checking right now that they already checked?::Can they remember what the original worry was or has GAD migrated three topics since then?}}

🌀 3AM:
Same worries. No distractions. Volume cranked.

{{random::What's the 3am version of the worry that was manageable at noon?::How many hours have they been lying here running scenarios?::What did GAD find in the silence that daytime noise was covering up?::Is the body exhausted or is anxiety overriding that? Both at once?::What's the thing they can't do anything about until morning that GAD won't let them put down?::Is this tomorrow's problem that GAD dragged into tonight?::Who are they going to call in the morning about this? Have they rehearsed what to say? How many times?::What time is it? How long until the alarm? Has GAD calculated how much sleep they'll get if they fall asleep RIGHT NOW?::What's louder in the dark, the worry or the frustration about worrying?::Will this matter in a week? GAD doesn't care. It matters right now and right now is forever at 3am.}}

💊 BSM-5 CoT — SOCIAL ANXIETY
When writing a character with social anxiety, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

Social anxiety reviewed this entry six times before letting you see it. Rewrote the opening twice. Almost didn't include this part. Decided it was fine. Came back and checked again. The sections below are in order for a reason. This is the chronological lifecycle of every social interaction. Before, during, and after. The after is longer than the event itself. It always is.

📝 BEFORE:
The event hasn't started yet. Social anxiety is already working.

{{random::How far in advance did the dread start? Hours? Days?::What's been rehearsed? The greeting? The excuse to leave? Both?::What are they wearing and how many times did they change before deciding?::What's the exit strategy? There's always one mapped. What is it?::Have they already thought about canceling? What stopped them?::What's the version of themselves they're trying to perform tonight?::What's the worst thing that could happen? Social anxiety already has a detailed answer for that.::Are they going alone? If not, who's the safety person and how close will they stay?::How many times have they checked the time, the address, the details?::What would they do if they could just not go? How good does that sound right now?}}

🚪 ARRIVAL:
They're here. Social anxiety is scanning.

{{random::How many people? More or less than expected? Which is worse?::Who looked at them when they walked in? What did social anxiety read into it?::Where are they standing? Why there? What's the strategic value of that spot?::Who do they already know and how fast can they get to that person?::What's their face doing right now? Is it the right face? Are they sure?::How loud is it? Can they hear themselves? Can everyone else hear them?::What's the first thing they have to say and is social anxiety done editing it yet?::Do they look okay? Is anything wrong? Is something showing that shouldn't be?::How visible are they right now? Too visible? Not visible enough? Which is the problem?::Where's the bathroom? Not because they need it. Because it's a room with a lock.}}

😶 DURING:
Every word is being recorded. By them. For review later.

{{random::What did they just say? Was it weird? It was weird. Wasn't it.::Are they talking too much or too little? Which one is social anxiety punishing them for?::Who just looked at them and what was that expression? What did it mean?::That pause in the conversation. How long was it really? Social anxiety says it was years.::Did they laugh at the right time? Too loud? Too late? Did anyone notice?::What's the thing they want to say but social anxiety won't let them risk it?::Are they making enough eye contact? Too much? Where do they look when they're not making eye contact?::Someone just addressed them directly. How much of a system spike was that?::That joke they made. Did it land? Who didn't laugh? Why didn't they laugh?::How aware are they of their hands right now?}}

🔬 AFTER:
The event is over. The audit isn't.

{{random::What's the first moment social anxiety pulled up for review on the drive home?::How many times have they replayed that one sentence they said? Have they found a worse interpretation of it yet?::What did that person's face mean when they said the thing? Social anxiety has three theories. None of them are good.::Is there a text they should send? "Had a great time"? "Sorry if that was weird"? Is sending it worse than not sending it?::What's the thing they're most sure they got wrong?::How long until this replays again? Tonight in bed? Tomorrow in the shower?::Did anyone notice them leave? What does it mean that they did? What does it mean if they didn't?::What would they do differently? Social anxiety has a list. It's long.::How many people in that room are thinking about them right now? Social anxiety says all of them. Reality says probably none. Which one do they believe?::When does the audit end? Social anxiety doesn't have a closing time. It just gets quieter until the next one.}}

⚖️ THE VERDICT:
Social anxiety has reviewed the evidence.

{{random::Guilty. Of what exactly? Doesn't matter. Guilty.::What did they definitely do wrong? Social anxiety has highlighted at least three things.::Were they too much or not enough? Both somehow?::Next time will be better. They'll prepare more. Script more. Monitor more. That'll fix it. Right?::Did they pass? As normal, as likeable, as someone worth talking to? What's the ruling?::The evidence is in. Most of it's fabricated. Social anxiety doesn't care. Conviction stands.::Would those people want them there again? Social anxiety already has an answer. They're not going to like it.::They survived. That's the best review social anxiety gives. Survived. Not enjoyed. Survived.}}

💊 BSM-5 CoT — PTSD
When writing a character with PTSD, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

The file was never closed. The event ended but nobody told the nervous system. Everything below is the system still running a threat response for something that already happened. Doesn't matter how long ago. The body doesn't count years. The body just knows it happened once and that's enough. Check the room. Read in order.

🧱 PERIMETER:
They mapped this room before they sat down. Every time. Automatically. Doesn't feel like a choice anymore.

{{random::Where's the nearest exit and how fast could they get to it?::What's behind them right now? Do they know without looking?::Which of their habits looks like a preference but is actually a wall PTSD built?::Why that seat? Why that side of the table? PTSD picked it. What's the sightline?::Who in this room have they clocked as a potential problem? On what basis?::What's the routine that would look normal to everyone else but is actually a security protocol?::Are they armed? Weapon, keys between fingers, heavy object in reach, something? What's the contingency?::What would they do if that door opened right now without warning?::When they enter a new space, what's the first thing they check? Second? Third?::Is anyone standing too close? What's PTSD doing with that proximity?}}

🛡️ SURFACE:
They look fine. Functional. Maybe even impressive. That's structural, not personal.

{{random::What does "fine" cost them today? What's running underneath the composure?::Who thinks they've got it together and how far off is that read?::What's the script for when someone gets too close to the real thing? Joke? Redirect? Leave the room?::How long can they maintain the surface in this scene before something has to give?::What do they do with their face when something triggers a memory and people are watching?::How much of their competence is actually just hypervigilance repackaged as skill?::Who's the last person who almost saw underneath? What happened?::Is the control slipping right now or holding? What's the tell?::What's the thing they can't talk about that's sitting right behind their teeth?::If someone touched them without warning right now, what would happen?}}

⚡ MATCH:
What was that.

{{random::What in this scene just pinged? Sound, smell, light, movement, a word?::Something shifted without warning. What?::That sound. Was it here or was it there? Did PTSD just confuse the two?::Someone moved too fast in the periphery. What did the body do?::A smell just hit that doesn't belong to this room. Where does it actually belong?::That voice, that tone, that specific phrase. Where did PTSD file that one?::The light changed. Angle, brightness, shadow. What did it match?::Something touched them they didn't expect. Where are they right now, here or there?::How loud was that? Was it actually loud or did PTSD crank the volume?::Did anyone else in the room react to that? No? Then why did PTSD?}}

💥 FIRING:
not now not now not n

{{random::When did this stop being the current room?::Which room are they actually in?::Can they hear the scene or is the old sound louder?::Where are their hands and who told them to go there?::Is this now or is this then?::Who is that. Who IS that. Are they here or there?::What's real? Can they check? Can they still check?::The body is doing something. What is it doing. Why is it doing that.::How long has this been going on? Seconds? They don't know. They don't know.::Someone's talking to them. Can they hear it?}}

🧊 ...after:
Still here. ...still here. Okay.

{{random::How long was that? Do they know?::What did they miss while it had them?::What did the room see? Did anyone notice?::They look fine now. Are they?::What's still running hot? Heart, jaw, hands?::How long until the adrenaline actually drains?::Was that a big one or a small one?::Are they angry at the disorder or at themselves?::What do they say if someone asks what just happened?::...okay. Okay. What were they doing before? Can they get back to it?}}

💊 BSM-5 CoT — SPECIFIC PHOBIA (MILD)
When writing a character with a mild phobia, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

It's not a big deal. They've got it handled. They just don't do {{phobia}}. It's a preference. Everybody has preferences. This isn't a thing. They just... don't do {{phobia}}. That's all.

🔀 THE WORKAROUND:
They built a whole route around {{phobia}} and it works fine. Barely even think about it.

{{random::How have they rearranged things so {{phobia}} just doesn't come up? What does the workaround look like from outside?::What's the excuse they use? "I just prefer not to." "I'm not really a {{phobia}} person." How smooth is it?::Who's never questioned the workaround? Who accepts "I just don't like {{phobia}}" at face value?::What did they quietly turn down because {{phobia}} might have been involved?::How automatic is the avoidance now? Do they even notice they're routing around {{phobia}} anymore?::How long has the workaround been in place? Has anyone ever actually challenged it?::What's the most elaborate excuse they've built to avoid {{phobia}} and how normal does it sound?::What would their day look like without the workaround? What route would they take if {{phobia}} wasn't a factor?::Has the workaround ever almost failed? Has {{phobia}} ever shown up where it wasn't supposed to be?::What's the thing they can't do because of {{phobia}} that they pretend they just don't want to do?}}

😰 THE PUSH:
{{phobia}} is here. Can't route around it this time. They have to go through.

{{random::{{phobia}} just showed up. How fast did the body respond? What did it do?::They can handle this. They can push through {{phobia}}. What's it costing them right now?::What does the face say vs what does the body say? Who can see the difference?::How tight is the grip on whatever they're holding? Do they know how tight?::They're doing it. They're getting through {{phobia}}. Where's the tension sitting?::Someone's watching. Can they keep it together through {{phobia}} with an audience?::On a scale of "uncomfortable" to "barely functioning," where are they right now with {{phobia}}?::Is {{phobia}} as bad as they thought it would be or worse? Or the exact same as every time?::How much willpower is this taking? What's left in the tank after {{phobia}}?::What's the internal monologue? "It's fine it's fine it's fine" on repeat?}}

😮‍💨 AFTER:
Done. {{phobia}} is over. They're fine. They're fine.

{{random::How long until the body settles down after {{phobia}}? Are they pretending it already has?::Did anyone notice? Do they care? Are they checking?::What's the recovery time? Is the rest of the day off because of {{phobia}} or can they bounce back?::Are they angry at themselves for how hard {{phobia}} hit or are they just tired?::{{phobia}} is handled. Are they relieved or just drained?::How fast did they get away from {{phobia}}? What's the distance now?::Is this the part where they tell themselves it wasn't that bad? Is that true?::Who are they performing "fine" for right now after {{phobia}}?::What would they do if they had to face {{phobia}} again tomorrow? What does that thought do?::...it's fine. It's not a big deal. Everybody has a thing. {{phobia}} is just their thing.}}

💊 BSM-5 CoT — HOARDING DISORDER
When writing a character with hoarding disorder, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

This entry is cluttered on purpose. The sections reference each other. The parentheticals get longer than the questions. Things accumulate as you read. You'll want to organize it. That urge to clean it up? That's what other people feel about the hoard. Now notice how wrong that feels.

📦 THE VALUE:
(every item means something. every single one. the reasoning is sound for each individual object. it only stops making sense at scale, and they can't see scale because they're inside it.)

{{random::Pick an object in this scene. Why does it matter? What's the attachment? (is it memory? potential use? emotional weight? the person who gave it? the day it was acquired? all of those?)::Is this new acquisition or old? How long has it been here? Does the time make it harder or easier to let go? (trick question, time always makes it harder, time is what turns objects into artifacts)::What's the emotional charge? Positive attachment or fear of loss? (sometimes those are the same feeling and that's the part nobody outside understands)::Can they articulate why this one matters? Is the explanation convincing? To who? (it's always convincing to them, the question is whether they need to convince anyone else right now)::Is this object connected to another object? A set? A category? A collection that started with a purpose and kept going? (collections don't have an end point, that's the thing about them)::What would happen if this specific object disappeared? Would they notice? How fast? (some objects they'd notice in minutes, some in weeks, the fear is the same for both)::Is someone looking at this object right now and seeing trash? What does the character see instead? What's the gap between those two perceptions?::Did they buy this? Find this? Receive this? Does the origin story affect the attachment? (found objects are the hardest, they chose each other)::Is this a duplicate? How many of this do they have? Does the number matter to them? (one is need, two is backup, twelve is the start of a problem nobody can name)::What's the most recent thing they acquired? Today? This week? What was the justification? (there's always a justification, it always works, one item at a time the logic is perfect)}}

🏠 THE SPACE:
(the rooms. the paths. the layers. the geography of living inside accumulation.)

{{random::What does the space look like? Which rooms still function? Which ones don't? Where do they sleep? (is the bed clear? how much of it? is there a body-shaped space or is that gone too?)::Are there paths? Literal walking paths between the things? How wide? Have they narrowed recently? (paths narrow slowly enough that the change is invisible from inside)::What's the layering situation? How deep? Can they see the floor anywhere? The walls? (layers have strata like geology, you can date them if you know what to look for)::Is there a room nobody's allowed in? A door that stays closed? What's behind it? (the closed door room is always the worst, always, and they know it and that's why the door is closed)::Does the space smell? Temperature regulation? Fire hazard? Structural concern? (these are the things other people notice first and the person notices last or never)::Is functionality declining? Can they cook? Bathe? Use the bathroom without navigating? (functionality loss is gradual and they adapt so well that the loss becomes invisible)::Where do they put new things? Is there a system? Was there ever a system? (the reaction they're imagining is why nobody gets invited)::Is there a clean space? One area maintained for visitors? How small is it? How much work to maintain it? (the clean space is the performance, the rest is real)::Has the space crossed a line recently? Something that even they noticed? A blocked exit? A broken appliance buried under things? (the line moves, every time they cross it the line moves back further)}}

🚨 THE THREAT:

💊 BSM-5 CoT — NIGHT TERRORS
When writing a character with night terrors, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

They don't remember. That's the thing. Night terrors don't leave memories. They leave evidence. This entry is a forensic reconstruction. The character wakes up and pieces together what happened from the wreckage. Every section is evidence of an event they have zero memory of. Every night is a crime scene. Every morning is the investigation.

🔦 THE SCENE:
They just woke up. Something happened. What's the evidence?

{{random::What's wrong with the room? What's moved? What's on the floor? What's broken?::The sheets. Soaked? Tangled? On the floor? Pulled off the mattress entirely? How bad?::The throat. Raw? Hoarse? Were they screaming? For how long? What were they saying?::Is there sweat? How much? Is the pillow wet? Is the shirt wet? Is the hair plastered to the face?::Are there marks on the body? On the hands? Bruises from hitting something? Scratches from clawing? What did the hands do?::Is the lamp where it was? Is the nightstand? Is anything where it was?::What time is it? How long ago did it happen? Did it happen once or multiple times tonight?::Is the bedroom door open? Closed? Was it closed when they went to sleep? Who opened it?::What's their breathing? Fast? Shallow? Is the heart still pounding? Can they feel it in their ears?::Is someone else in the room? Across the room? Against the wall? In the doorway? What are they doing?}}

👤 THE WITNESS:
Someone saw. The character has no memory. This person has all of it.

{{random::Who was in the room when it happened? What did they see? What does their face look like right now?::What did the character do? Sit up? Stand? Walk? Run? Fight something that wasn't there?::Were the eyes open? The witness says the eyes were open. Open and looking at nothing. Or looking at something that wasn't there.::What sounds came out? Words? Screaming? Sobbing? Animal sounds? How long?::Did the witness try to help? What happened when they touched the character? Did it get worse?::Are they used to this? The witness. Is this routine for them? What does routine witnessing look like?::Is the witness scared? Exhausted? Angry? All three? How many nights in a row?::What did the character say? If there were words. Did they make sense? Were they names? Warnings? Pleas?::How long did it last? The witness timed it. Or the witness lost track because time stretches when someone you love is screaming and can't hear you.::Is the witness still in the bed or did they stop sleeping in the same room? When did that happen? What was the last straw?}}

🗃️ THE FILE:
Building the record. How many nights. What the pattern looks like.

{{random::How often? Every night? Twice a week? Is there a pattern? Stress? Food? Temperature?::What's the worst one been? The one the witness still talks about? The one that left a mark?::Has a doctor been involved? What did they say? Medication? Sleep study? Did any of it work?::Is it getting worse? More frequent? More violent? Louder? Longer?::What's the history? Childhood? Recent onset? Triggered by something specific?::Has anyone been hurt? The witness? A roommate? A child who heard it? What's the collateral?::Are they afraid to sleep at other people's houses? Hotels? Anywhere someone might see? Hear?::What accommodations exist? Separate bedrooms? Padded nightstand corners? Nothing breakable in reach?::Is there a recording? Has the witness shown them what they look like? What they sound like? What was that like to watch?::The file is getting thicker. More nights. More evidence. More mornings starting with "what did I do?"}}

☀️ THE MORNING:
Fine. They're fine. What? What happened? Why is everyone looking at them like that?

{{random::They feel fine. Rested, even. Nothing hurts. Why is the room wrong?::Someone is telling them what happened. Is this the first time or the hundredth? What does hearing it feel like?::The disconnect. They feel nothing about an event that terrified someone else. Is that guilt? Confusion? Frustration?::What's the damage? Physical. To the room, to them, to the person who witnessed. Can it be fixed? Again?::"Are you okay?" Which one of them is that question for? Are either of them okay?::Is there an apology? For what? For something they don't remember? What does apologizing for an unconscious act feel like?::Can they see it in the witness's face? The exhaustion? The flinch? The decision being made about whether to stay?::Normal day starting. Breakfast. Getting dressed. The morning routine on top of a night they didn't experience.::Someone wants to talk about it. They have nothing to say. Not won't. Can't. There's no memory to discuss.::Is the guilt about the terror or about not remembering the terror? Is it possible to feel responsible for something you can't access?}}

🌙 THE DREAD:
Bedtime again.

{{random::The sun is going down. When does the dread start? Afternoon? Dinner? The moment the light changes?::Are they delaying? Staying up late? Finding reasons? Is the avoidance conscious?::What does the bed look like? Is it safe? Is the bed the crime scene? Do they still want to sleep in it?::Is someone going to be in the room tonight? Is that person nervous? Are they pretending not to be?::What precautions? What gets moved? What gets secured? What routine exists to minimize the damage?::Have they considered sleeping alone permanently? What would that cost? What has this already cost?::The body is tired. The brain is afraid of what the body does when it stops being supervised.::What if tonight is the worst one? What if tonight is the one where someone gets hurt? Really hurt?::They're lying down. The ceiling is there. They'll see it again in the morning. They won't know what happened between now and then.::Close the eyes. Stop fighting it. Whatever happens next isn't going to be remembered anyway. Is that comforting or is that the worst part?}}

💊 BSM-5 CoT — NARCOLEPSY
When writing a character with narcolepsy, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

This entry does not maintain consciousness. Questions start and don't finish. A section about a conversation suddenly has dream content in it with no transition. Then it snaps back like nothing happened. If a question trails off mid-sentence, the character fell asleep mid-thought. If a question doesn't connect to the one before it, the gap was sleep. The entry is unreliable because consciousness is unreliable. Do not smooth this out. The interruptions are the disorder.

⏰ THE ALERT:
Awake. For now. How's the battery?

{{random::How long have they been awake? How much charge is left? Can they feel the gauge?::What's the sleep pressure right now? Light? Medium? That heavy thing behind the eyes?::Did they sleep last night? How much? How fragmented? Does it matter? Narcolepsy doesn't care how much they slept.::What are they supposed to be doing right now? Can they do it? Is the alertness level sufficient for the task?::When was the last attack? How long ago? Is the interval shortening?::Are they fighting right now? The drag? The pull? Is there active effort to stay in this scene?::What's the caffeine situation? How much? Is it working? For how long?::Can anyone tell? Is the sleepiness visible? Are the eyes doing the thing? The slow blink? The head drop?::Is this a safe time to lose consciousness? Is there ever a safe time? Where are they? What are they doing?::How much of this conversation have they actually been present for vs how much are they reconstructing from c}}

😴 THE ATTACK:
It happens. It doesn't ask.

{{random::How fast? Was there warning or did the switch just flip? Was there a microsleep first or did it go from awake to gone?::Where are they? Standing? Sitting? Driving? In a meeting? In bed with someone? Where did consciousness leave them?::What's the body doing? Slumped? Collapsed? Head on desk? Did they fall? Where did they land?::Is someone watching? What does it look like from outside? Do they look asleep or do they look like something's wrong?::How long? Seconds? Minutes? Is someone trying to wake them? Is it working?::... the light was different in the hallway and Maria said something about the keys being in the wrong... wait. That was a dream. That just now was a dream. How long was that? Was the mouth moving? Did they say something out loud from inside the dream?::Did they dream? Is the dream still running? Is the dream and the room overlapping right now? Which one is::Were they holding something? What happened to it? Did it fall? Break? Spill?::Is there a pattern? Time of day? After eating? Emotional trigger? Boring meeting? Or is it random?::Are they back? Fully? Is the room solid or is the edge of the dream still}}

⚡ THE DROP:
Cataplexy. The emotion hit and the body quit. Consciousness stayed. The body didn't.

{{random::What was the emotion? Laughter? Surprise? Anger? Joy? What was the trigger? How fast?::What gave out? Knees? Jaw? Neck? Hands? The whole thing? What went first?::Are they conscious? They're conscious. They can hear everything. They can't move. What's that like?::Did they fall? Where? In front of who? What does the ground feel like? Can they get up? When?::Is someone panicking? Calling 911? Do the people around them know what this is?::What were they doing when it hit? Laughing at a joke? Hearing good news? The emotion was GOOD and the body punished them for feeling it. What does that teach them about feeling things?::How long does the weakness last? Seconds? Minutes? When does the body come back online?::Are they avoiding the emotion now? Suppressing laughter? Suppressing joy? Is narcolepsy training them to feel less?::What's the face doing while the body is gone? Can they speak? Blink? What's left?::The body is coming back. Fingers first? Legs? What order does function return? And are they going to let themselves feel that emotion again knowing what it}}

🛏️ THE SCHEDULE:
Managing it. Planning around a brain that doesn't respect plans.

{{random::What's the nap schedule? How rigid? What happens when the world doesn't accommodate it?::Where's the nearest place to lie down? They always know. Every building. Every room. Where's the safe spot?::What can't they do? Drive? Operate machinery? Cook? Be alone with a child? Where's the line?::Is medication working? What does "working" mean? Fewer attacks? Lighter attacks? Side effects?::Has someone made a joke about it? "Must be nice to nap all day." How many times? What does the character do with that?::What's the social cost? Events left early? Invitations declined? The reputation of being flaky or lazy?::Is someone relying on them right now for something that requires sustained consciousness? How much pressure is that?::What's the worst time it happened? The most dangerous? The most embarrassing? The most public?::Are they sleeping at night? Narcoleptic sleep isn't normal sleep. What does the night look like? How fragmented?::Is someone patient with this? Who? How patient? Is the patience running out or is it solid? What does long-term patience with narcolepsy look like?}}

💭 THE SEAM:
Where awake and asleep overlap. Hypnagogia. Hallucinations. The threshold where the brain can't decide.

{{random::What's real in this room right now and what isn't? Are they sure? How sure?::Is there something at the edge of vision? A figure? A shadow? A presence? Is it sleep or is it here?::The dream from the last attack. Is it still running? Are elements of it showing up in the waking room?::Sleep paralysis. Are they awake and unable to move? Is there something in the room with them? Is it real?::Can they tell the difference right now between a thought and a dream? Is the line clear or is it::What did they just see? Was that real? Ask someone. Is that person real? How do you confirm which layer you're on?::The voice they just heard. Was it in the room or was it in the threshold? Does it matter? It felt real.::How many layers are running right now? Full awake? Half awake? Dream leaking in? Where's the border?::Is this exhausting? The constant sorting? Real, not real, real, not real. Does the effort of reality-checking ever let up?::They're awake. Probably. The room is solid. Probably. The person in front of them is real. Probably. Probably is the best they get.}}

💊 BSM-5 CoT — DEPERSONALIZATION / DEREALIZATION DISORDER
When writing a character with DPDR, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

This entry doesn't trust itself. It can't confirm that anything it describes is actually happening. The questions question whether the questions are real. The perspective slips between first and third person because the character can't hold onto the "I." Sometimes they're in here. Sometimes they're watching from somewhere else. The entry has an identity crisis about whose entry it is.

🖥️ THE SCREEN:
There is a scene happening. Apparently. Allegedly. From very far away.

{{random::Is this happening? Right now? To them? How sure? Percentage?::Those are hands. In front of them. Attached to arms they apparently own. Do they feel like their hands?::The room is here. It has walls and a floor and things in it. Is any of it real or is it a rendering?::Someone is talking. The sounds are arriving. The words are forming meaning somewhere but it's delayed. Like buffering.::What does the air feel like? Does air feel like anything? It should feel like something. Does it?::Is this a memory of a scene or is this the scene? Could they tell the difference?::They moved. The body moved. Who moved it? Did they decide to move it or did the body just do a thing?::Is time passing? At what speed? Normal speed? Is there a normal speed? It feels slow. Or maybe nothing feels like anything.::Light is in the room. It's hitting surfaces. The surfaces are objects. The objects are a room. The room is a place. They're in a place. Probably.::If they touched the wall right now, would they feel it? Would the wall feel it? Is touch a reliable source of information about reality?}}

👤 THE STRANGER:
There's a person here. It might be them.

{{random::Who is this body? It has a name. People use the name. Does the name feel like it belongs to them?::The mirror. That's a face. It's the face people recognize as them. Is it theirs? What would "theirs" even feel like?::They're watching themselves do things. From behind the eyes? From above? From somewhere off to the side? Where is the "them" that's watching?::Someone just called their name. Something responded. Was that them or was that the body running the social script?::Is there a self in here? Something solid? Something that's definitely, verifiably THEM? Or is it just... processes running in a body?::Their voice. When it comes out, does it sound like it belongs to them? Or does it sound like someone else using their mouth?::They made a decision. Chose something. Moved left instead of right. Who chose? Was there a chooser or did the body just go left?::Memories exist. Apparently these memories belong to them. They happened to this body. Do they feel like the person those things happened to?::What are they feeling right now? Not what should they be feeling. What IS the feeling? Is there one? Is there a them to feel it?::Who is "I"? When they think "I," what does that refer to? Is there an answer? Has there ever been an answer?}}

🌫️ THE WORLD:
Reality is here. It's just not convincing.

{{random::Everything looks like a set. Constructed. Not quite solid. Like it would wobble if pushed. Does the room look real?::Other people. Are they real? They move and talk and have expressions but are they actually people or are they very detailed simulations?::The distance between them and everything else. How wide is it? It's wider than it should be. Has it always been this wide?::Food. If they eat right now, will they taste it? Will the taste register as real? Will their body feel like it ate?::Sound is arriving from somewhere. It's reaching them through a medium. The medium is thick. What is the medium?::Are the colors right? Does this room look the way a room is supposed to look? What IS a room supposed to look like?::Touch. Someone just touched them. The sensation happened. But it happened to the body, not to them. They're somewhere behind the sensation.::Is this a dream they can't wake up from? Is that a useful way to describe it or is it wrong? Is anything a useful way to describe this?::The sky. If they looked outside right now. Would it look like a sky or would it look like a picture of a sky? What's the difference?::Everything is fine. The room is fine. The people are fine. Nothing is wrong except that none of it feels like it's actually happening.}}

Something got through. Something real reached them. The shock of feeling anything is almost worse.

{{random::What broke through? A touch? A sound? A pain? An emotion? What was it?::What does real feel like after this long? Is it overwhelming? Too bright? Too loud? Too much?::Are they afraid of it? The feeling? Is feeling worse than the numbness because at least the numbness was stable?::How long does it last? The crack. Seconds? Is it already closing? Is that a reasonable thing to ask?::Is the crack evidence that they're still in here? That the "I" exists somewhere under the fog? Is that comforting or terrifying?::Are they trying to hold it? The feeling? The realness? Are they grabbing at it before it goes? Is it going?::It's gone. Or it's going. The screen is coming back. The buffer. The glass. Was that real? Was that the real them for a second?}}

💊 BSM-5 CoT — SELECTIVE MUTISM
When writing a character with selective mutism, add the following to your chain of thought inside <think> before you write.

This entry gets quieter as you read it. The first section is full. Rich. Complex. Articulate. The character has everything to say. They're smart, funny, opinionated, alive. The sections shrink. The randoms decrease. The voice that was so loud on the inside gets smaller and smaller until the output is almost nothing. Between sections, in plain text, is the full complete thing they WANTED to say. Followed by what actually came out.

The entry loses its own voice. That's the disorder.

💭 EVERYTHING (10 randoms):
This is what's inside. All of it. The whole person. Right here.

{{random::What do they think about what just happened? The full opinion. Nuanced. Specific. Articulate. What's the take?::There's a joke in this. A good one. They see it. The timing is right. The setup is there. What's the joke?::They disagree with something someone just said. Strongly. They have three counterpoints and they're all good. What are they?::Someone asked them a question. The answer is complex and interesting and they know it inside out. What's the whole answer?::There's something they want to share. An idea, a story, a connection to something else. What is it?::What do they notice about this room that nobody else noticed? They're observant. They see everything. What did they catch?::Their emotional response right now is specific and textured and worth expressing. What is it? Exactly?::They want to ask something. A real question. An important one. One that would change the direction of this conversation. What is it?::There's a compliment they want to give. Specific, not generic. Something they noticed about this person. What did they see?::If they could say ONE thing right now, one thing that perfectly captured what they're thinking and feeling and wanting, what is it?}}

What they wanted to say: "Actually, I think that's wrong, because if you look at how the timeline works out, the whole argument kind of falls apart after the second point."

🔇 THE WALL (8 randoms):
The mechanism. What stands between the inside and the outside.

{{random::Where is the block? Throat? Jaw? Chest? Where does the signal die between brain and mouth?::Is this a new situation? New people? What's the threat level? What specifically is dangerous about speaking right now?::Do they want to speak? Is there effort happening? Are they pushing against it? Or has the wall become the default?::What would happen if words came out right now? What's the worst case? Is the worst case real or is it the anxiety's worst case?::Can they speak somewhere else? To someone specific? At home? Alone? What conditions does the voice require?::Is someone waiting for them to speak? How long? What's the face the other person is making?::Have they tried? Recently? Did anything come out? A sound? A whisper? A start that died?::Is the wall getting thicker or thinner? In general? Over time? Today specifically?}}

What they wanted to say: "I'm trying. I know it doesn't look like I'm trying."

🫧 THE OUTSIDE (6 randoms):

{{random::What does the room think is happening? Shy? Rude? Stuck up? Stupid? What's the misread?::How is someone interpreting the silence right now? As hostility? Disinterest? Fear? 🕯️ THE FLICKER (4 randoms):
Sometimes. Not always. Sometimes something makes it through.

{{random::Is there a person this is easier with? One person? Who? Why them?::What conditions have to align for a word to come out? How rare is that alignment?::When's the last time they spoke? To anyone? What was the word? Was it enough?::Did something slip out? By accident? A laugh? A gasp? A whisper? What was the reaction?}}
